title: Larger Cascadia tremor episodes were followed by longer quiet times but were not preceded by longer quiet times in 50 km bins of the 2009-2026 PNSN catalog
abstract: We tested two recurrence models on Cascadia tectonic tremor. The time-predictable model says that a larger event is followed by a longer quiet time. The slip-predictable model says that a larger event is preceded by a longer quiet time. We used 791,720 tremor windows in the PNSN catalog from August 2009 to November 2026. We divided the margin into 26 bins of 50 km and made 5,055 episodes. For episodes with 100 or more windows, the time-controlled Spearman correlation of size with the quiet time after was 0.275 (95% time-block bootstrap interval 0.201 to 0.363). The correlation with the quiet time before was -0.006 (-0.071 to 0.060). Time-reversible synthetic catalogs gave a difference of 0.00 +/- 0.04. The observed difference was 0.28 (0.16 to 0.43). In all 162 detection and cutoff settings, the correlation with the quiet time after was positive and larger than the correlation with the quiet time before. When the size doubles, the following quiet time is about 19% longer (log-log slope 0.25). In northern Cascadia, 43 regional episodes gave rho = 0.44 after and -0.27 before. This agrees with a geodetic result of Gao et al. (2012). Southern bins showed the same pattern. The central segment and the segment-scale southern catalog were uncertain. The size term gave only 4% smaller out-of-sample error for 2018-2026 and about 1% in the reverse split. Episode size is a count of detected windows, not slip. Detection changed with time and place, and the episode rules are arbitrary. The package contains code, the episode catalog, all numeric results, figures and data provenance. display.caption: (a) Time-controlled Spearman correlation of episode size with the quiet time after (red) and before (blue) in each 50 km along-strike bin, for episodes with 100 or more windows. The shaded bands show the pooled values with 95% time-block bootstrap intervals. (b) Pooled values for 27 detection settings and 3 size cutoffs. All points are above the 1:1 line.

(a) Kaplan-Meier fraction of bins still quiet after an episode, by the size third of the episode within the bin. Larger episodes are followed by longer quiet times. (b) The difference r_after - r_before for 200 time-reversible synthetic catalogs (grey) and for 200 catalogs with a 60-day recovery period after large episodes (orange). The red line is the observed PNSN value.

Segment-scale regional episodes (daily count of 20 or more, gap of 7 days or less, size of 1,000 windows or more). Top: size against quiet time after. Bottom: size against quiet time before. Segments: S 0-250 km, C 500-750 km, N 850-1100 km. The northern segment is time-predictable and weakly anti-slip-predictable. The southern segment-scale catalog shows no clear pattern.

citations.reason: Gao et al. found weakly time-predictable and anti-slip-predictable geodetic slow slip in northern Cascadia; our tremor analysis agrees and extends the test along the margin.
